name: How do you waterproof a shower or wet room before setting porcelain tile?

mainEntity.name: How do you waterproof a shower or wet room before setting porcelain tile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain tile is completely waterproof on its own, but the grout joints and substrate underneath are vulnerable unless a certified waterproof system is used. For walk-in showers, tub surrounds, and wet rooms, installers mount cement backer boards or foam waterproof panels, tape all seams with alkali-resistant mesh, and apply a liquid waterproofing membrane or sheet membrane. The shower pan requires pre-sloping and liner testing before any tile is laid. This multi-layered barrier ensures water drains properly without penetrating framing, drywall, or subfloors.
acceptedAnswer.description: Waterproofing requires cement backer panels, taped seams, and a continuous liquid or sheet membrane behind the tile to stop water from reaching the framing.
